core_obligations: In the case where each (K_n^p) is right acyclic for lim, use the computation lemma to get the short exact sequence 0 -> lim_n K^p_n -> prod_n K^p_n -> prod_n K^p_n -> 0 for every p (proof lines 23283-23288).
Use that the complex with terms lim_n K^p_n computes R lim K, again by the computation lemma, to conclude the lemma in this case (proof lines 23289-23291).
For general K, use the computation lemma to find a quasi-isomorphism K -> L in D(Ab(N)) such that each (L_n^p) is acyclic (proof lines 23294-23296).
Use that products are exact in the category of abelian groups to conclude that prod K_n^bullet is quasi-isomorphic to prod L_n^bullet (proof lines 23296-23297).
Conclude that the result for L, already proved, implies the result for K (proof lines 23298-23299).
difficulty_reason: The lemma takes an object K = (K_n^bullet) of the derived category of the inverse systems of abelian groups and asserts the existence of a canonical distinguished triangle R lim K -> prod_n K_n^bullet -> prod_n K_n^bullet -> R lim K[1] in D(Ab), which says precisely that R lim K is a derived limit of the inverse system in the sense of the derived-category definition (source lines 23269-23280). The proof splits into a special case and a reduction. In the special case where each inverse system (K_n^p) is right acyclic for lim, the computation lemma gives a short exact sequence 0 -> lim_n K^p_n -> prod_n K^p_n -> prod_n K^p_n -> 0 for every p, and since the complex with terms lim_n K^p_n computes R lim K, the lemma holds in that case (proof lines 23283-23291). The substantive step is the reduction: for general K, the computation lemma provides a quasi-isomorphism K -> L in D(Ab(N)) such that each (L_n^p) is acyclic, and because products are exact in the category of abelian groups the product prod K_n^bullet is quasi-isomorphic to prod L_n^bullet; hence the result for L, already proved, implies the result for K (proof lines 23294-23299). The non-routine content is the passage from the acyclic case to the general one using the existence of a suitable replacement and the exactness of products.
